measured: re-read against the applications in scope (the Volter products and Dub, Rallly, Twenty, LibreChat, Cal.com) at the demand scan's commits (twin-world generated/demand.json). Two name Hugging Face. Browser Substrate (3116b2e) names huggingface.co only in scripts/prepare-localrouter-pack.mjs:88, a maintainer's script that writes the model page's URL into a pack's provenance and calls nothing: not demand. volter-ai/localrouter (107fb5d) depends on @huggingface/transformers, whose tokenizers load from the cached files only (engine/node-loader.mjs:80 and engine/embeddings.mjs:338, local_files_only), so the library calls nothing; its scripts, lab/ probes and tests are not demand. Its model cache downloads each artifact of its catalog (docs/artifacts/*.json: a repository, a PINNED commit sha, and per file its path, url, size and sha256) from https://huggingface.co/<repo>/resolve/<commit>/<path>, following redirects, resuming a partial file with Range: bytes=<offset>- and If-Range: <the validator it kept: ETag, else Last-Modified>, taking 200, 206 (its Content-Range and Content-Length checked) and a 416 at a complete offset, then checking the sha256. No token is sent: the models are public. No twin-world package, cookbook, script or other pack of twin-packs-p3 calls the Hub. Because the revisions are real commits, a World holds the real repository: it is seeded by creating it (the API) and pushing it (git over HTTP, the LFS objects by git-lfs's batch API), as a person publishes a model to the Hub.
